answers.quote: The shortest distance measured from the initial to the final position of an object is known as the displacement.
answers.notes: Direct definition in claim.

answers.quote: The shortest distance measured from the initial to the final position of an object is known as the displacement.
answers.notes: Initial and final positions coincide, so shortest distance (displacement) is zero by c01; not stated verbatim.

answers.quote: The average speed of an object is obtained by dividing the total distance travelled by the total time taken.
answers.notes: Average speed = 100 km / 2 h = 50 km/h by c05.

answers.quote: Velocity is the speed of an object moving in a definite direction.
answers.notes: Velocity is speed in a definite direction (c04); speed is distance per unit time (c03).

answers.quote: As the object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in uniform motion.
answers.notes: Statement 1 is c02. Statement 2 false: displacement is the shortest distance (c01), so it cannot exceed distance travelled.

answers.quote: The acceleration of an object is the change in velocity per unit time.
answers.notes: Direct definition in claim.

answers.quote: The acceleration of an object is the change in velocity per unit time.
answers.notes: a = change in velocity / time = 20/300 = 1/15 m/s^2 by c06.

answers.answer: প্রতি মুহূর্তে দিক বদলায় বলে বেগ বদলাতে থাকে
answers.quote: The motion of the athlete moving along a circular path is, therefore, an example of an accelerated motion.
answers.notes: Claim states circular motion at constant speed is accelerated because direction of velocity keeps changing.

answers.quote: If you carefully note, on being released the stone moves along a straight line tangential to the circular path.
answers.notes: Direct statement in claim.

answers.quote: When an object moves along a straight line with uniform acceleration, it is possible to relate its velocity, acceleration during motion and the distance covered by it in a certain time interval by a set of equations known as the equations of motion.
answers.notes: not covered by claims — claims only say the equations of motion exist (c07); none of the three equation forms is given.

answers.quote: The acceleration of an object is the change in velocity per unit time.
answers.notes: not covered by claims — only D (acceleration = change in velocity / time, c06) is in the claims; the equation forms for A and B and the v = 2πr/t formula for C are not given.

answers.quote: In other words, all objects resist a change in their state of motion. In a qualitative way, the tendency of undisturbed objects to stay at rest or to keep moving with the same velocity is called inertia. This is why, the first law of motion is also known as the law of inertia.
answers.notes: First law is also known as the law of inertia.

answers.quote: An opposite experience is encountered when we are standing in a bus and the bus begins to move suddenly. Now we tend to fall backwards. This is because the sudden start of the bus brings motion to the bus as well as to our feet in contact with the floor of the bus. But the rest of our body opposes this motion because of its inertia.
answers.notes: Claim describes passengers falling backwards when a bus starts suddenly.

answers.quote: Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion or of rest. The mass of an object is a measure of its inertia.
answers.notes: Mass is a measure of inertia.

answers.answer: ঘর্ষণ বল ঠেলার বলকে ভারসাম্য করে দেয়
answers.quote: This friction force arises between two surfaces in contact; in this case, between the bottom of the box and floor's rough surface. It balances the pushing force and therefore the box does not move.
answers.notes: Claim states friction balances the pushing force so the box does not move.

answers.answer: একবার চলতে শুরু করা বস্তুকে চালিয়ে রাখা, থামানো বস্তুকে নাড়ানোর চেয়ে সহজ
answers.quote: It is found experimentally that µk is less than µs.
answers.notes: µk < µs (c21) means kinetic friction is smaller, so keeping a moving body moving is easier; the verbal conclusion is inferred, not quoted.

answers.quote: But the rest of the body continues to move forward due to inertia. We are thrown forward.
answers.notes: Claim: feet stop due to friction but rest of body continues forward due to inertia.

answers.quote: Momentum of a body is defined to be the product of its mass m and velocity v, and is denoted by p: p = m v
answers.notes: Direct formula in claim.

answers.answer: যে বল ১ কেজি ভরের বস্তুতে ১ মি/সে² ত্বরণ সৃষ্টি করে
answers.quote: In SI unit force is one that causes an acceleration of 1 m s-2 to a mass of 1 kg. This unit is known as newton : 1 N = 1 kg m s-2
answers.notes: Direct definition of the newton in claim.

answers.answer: বল থামার সময় বাড়িয়ে আঘাতের বল কমাতে
answers.quote: In doing so, the fielder increases the time during which the high velocity of the moving ball decreases to zero. Thus, the acceleration of the ball is decreased and therefore the impact of catching the fast moving ball is also reduced.
answers.notes: Pulling hands back increases time, decreases acceleration and impact (c28).

answers.quote: In SI unit force is one that causes an acceleration of 1 m s-2 to a mass of 1 kg. This unit is known as newton : 1 N = 1 kg m s-2
answers.notes: Unit-force (newton) definition c25 and force measurement c26 sit in the second-law material, but no claim explicitly attributes the unit definition to a named law; first law is the generic definition of force in some texts.

answers.quote: The SI unit of momentum is kilogram metre per second (kg m s-1).
answers.notes: Statement 1 is c29; statement 2 is c27 (impulse = change in momentum).

answers.quote: Action and reaction act on different bodies and so they cannot be cancelled out.
answers.notes: Action and reaction act on different bodies and so cannot be cancelled out.

answers.quote: When a gun is fired, it exerts a forward force on the bullet. The bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun. This results in the recoil of the gun.
answers.notes: Gun/bullet equal and opposite forces (c33) are the third law (c30/c31).

answers.answer: আমরা রাস্তাকে পিছনে ঠেলি এবং রাস্তা আমাদের পায়ে সমান ও বিপরীত বল দিয়ে সামনে ঠেলে
answers.quote: you push the road below backwards. The road exerts an equal and opposite force on your feet to make you move forward.
answers.notes: Direct statement in claim.

answers.quote: In all collisions the total linear momentum is conserved; the initial momentum of the system is equal to the final momentum of the system.
answers.notes: In all collisions total linear momentum is conserved.

answers.answer: পৃথিবীর ভর বিশাল বলে একই বলে তার ত্বরণ নগণ্য হয়
answers.quote: which shows that force is proportional to the product of mass m and acceleration a.
answers.notes: Inferred from F = ma (c24) with equal force (c37): Earth's huge mass makes its acceleration negligible; not stated verbatim in claims.

answers.notes: Recoil from equal and opposite bullet/gun forces (c33) is the third law; other pairs mismatch the claims.

answers.notes: Direct value in claim.

answers.notes: Weight on moon = 1/6 of weight on earth.

answers.quote: Therefore the magnitude of the gravitational force F will be equal to the product of mass and acceleration due to the gravitational force, that is, F = m g
answers.notes: Weight = mg = 10 x 9.8 = 98 N (c43, weight is a force c44).

answers.quote: The motion of the moon around the earth is due to the centripetal force. The centripetal force is provided by the force of attraction of the earth.
answers.notes: Centripetal force for the moon is provided by the earth's force of attraction.

answers.quote: Every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force which is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
answers.notes: Force is inversely proportional to square of distance; doubling distance gives 1/4.

answers.notes: A Cavendish c38; B pascal c50; C newton c45; D free fall c41.

answers.answer: বল প্রয়োগ ও বস্তুর সরণ — দুটোই থাকতে হবে
answers.quote: two conditions need to be satisfied for work to be done: (i) a force should act on an object, and (ii) the object must be displaced.
answers.notes: Two conditions for work: force acts and object is displaced.

answers.quote: Let W be the work done. We define work to be equal to the product of the force and displacement. Work done = force × displacement
answers.notes: Work = force x displacement = 5 x 2 = 10 J.

answers.quote: Our electricity bills carry the energy consumption in units of kWh. Note that kWh is a unit of energy and not of power.
answers.notes: kWh is a unit of energy, not power.

answers.quote: There is another unit of power, namely the horsepower (hp) 1 hp = 746 W

If we assume that the moon's orbits around the earth is perfectly circular then the earth's gravitational force does no work. The moon's instantaneous displacement is tangential while the earth's force is radially inwards
answers.notes: Claim covers the analogous moon case: gravitational force does no work in a perfectly circular orbit; applied here to a planet.

answers.quote: Thus, the kinetic energy possessed by an object of mass, m and moving with a uniform velocity, v is Ek = 1/2 mv2 (Eq. 10.5)
answers.notes: Derived from claims: p = mv (c22) and Ek = 1/2 mv^2 (c60) give p^2 = 2mEk, so at equal Ek the heavier body has more momentum; not stated verbatim.

answers.answer: A ও R উভয়ই সত্য এবং R হল A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: Not all forces are conservative. Friction, for example, is a nonconservative force.
answers.notes: Friction is nonconservative (c68); conservative work depends only on initial/final positions (c67), which is why friction's path dependence makes it nonconservative — the path-dependence of friction itself is implied, not quoted.
